NVDA.text: Nvidia rose about 0.5% with the broader technology and AI trade as tame producer-price data eased rate concerns; no distinct Nvidia-specific catalyst was confirmed.

AVGO.text: Broadcom rose about 0.4% with the broader technology and semiconductor tape as tame producer-price data supported risk appetite; no distinct company-specific catalyst was confirmed.

TSM.text: TSM edged up about 0.3% with the broader AI and semiconductor trade as tame producer-price data eased rate concerns; no fresh TSM-specific catalyst was confirmed.

ASML.text: ASML rose about 2.1% as semiconductor-equipment shares remained supported by expanding AI-related fab spending, including Intel's newly enlarged capital raise, while the broader tech market advanced.

KLAC.text: KLA rose about 0.5% with semiconductor and AI-infrastructure shares as tame producer-price data supported the broader technology rally; no distinct KLA-specific catalyst was confirmed.

INTC.text: Intel rose about 3.6%, extending its rebound as investors absorbed the upsized $20 billion equity raise intended to support foundry and AI investment, while semiconductor shares benefited from the broader tech rally.

MU.text: Micron jumped about 4.2% as Sandisk's strong long-term growth outlook reinforced expectations for sustained AI-driven memory demand, helping memory-chip shares outperform during Thursday's technology rally.

DDOG.text: Datadog rebounded about 4.7% with enterprise-software strength, recovering further from last week's earnings-driven selloff; no fresh company-specific catalyst was confirmed Thursday.

META.text: Meta rose about 2.8% as communication-services and mega-cap technology shares advanced after tame producer-price data eased rate concerns; no distinct Meta-specific catalyst was confirmed.

PLTR.text: Palantir gained about 4.7%, extending its earnings-driven breakout as enterprise-software shares remained strong and the broader Nasdaq advanced; no new Palantir-specific catalyst was confirmed.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell about 3.3% with no confirmed negative operating catalyst; trading remained volatile after its recent rebound and the post-lockup increase in tradable shares, while Musk disclosed a 48.4% stake.
